target.name: Relaxin receptors
target.description: Relaxin family peptides are insulin-related heterodimeric hormones that act through four G protein-coupled receptors, and this ligand-receptor system governs reproductive physiology, connective tissue remodelling and aspects of appetite and stress behaviour. Relaxin-2, the main circulating form in humans, signals through RXFP1 to soften and remodel collagen-rich tissues such as the cervix and pubic symphysis, promote vasodilation and increased renal blood flow in pregnancy, and restrain fibrosis.

target.name: dGMP catabolic process
target.description: Breakdown of dGMP disposes of deoxyguanosine monophosphate arising from DNA turnover and from the deoxynucleotide pool, keeping precursor supply balanced and preventing the nucleotide imbalances that distort replication fidelity. Cytosolic 5'-nucleotidases remove the phosphate to give deoxyguanosine, which guanine deaminase converts toward xanthine, and xanthine dehydrogenase completes oxidation to urate for excretion; a nucleotide N-glycosidase offers an alternative route that cleaves the base directly from the sugar phosphate.

target.name: metanephric nephron tubule morphogenesis
target.description: The metanephros is the permanent adult kidney, and shaping its nephron tubules is how filtrate-processing epithelium acquires its final form: a continuous, correctly segmented and properly lumenized tube running from glomerulus to collecting duct. Metanephric nephron tubule morphogenesis converts induced mesenchyme-derived renal vesicles into elongated, polarized epithelial tubules, so that failures here produce hypoplastic or dysplastic kidneys, cystic disease and reduced nephron endowment with lifelong consequences for blood filtration and salt and water balance.

target.name: prolactin signaling pathway
target.description: Prolactin is a pituitary peptide hormone best known for driving mammary gland development and milk production, and it also acts on the ovary, prostate, liver and immune cells. Signalling begins when prolactin binds its single-chain cytokine-family receptor, which dimerizes and, through associated Janus kinases, activates STAT transcription factors as well as Ras-MAPK and PI3K routes, ending in changes to transcription of milk protein, proliferation and survival genes.
